requirements.requirement: Establish a private network between node1 and node2 that excludes node3
requirements.summary: node1 and node2 each have an eth1 NIC not present on node3; static 10.10.10.0/24 addressing was configured on both (node1 via UCI network.priv, node2 via ifcfg-eth1) and ping connectivity was confirmed over eth1. node3 has no second NIC and cannot reach this segment.

requirements.requirement: node2's HTTP service on port 8080 stays on the private network only (not reachable from the management network)
requirements.summary: The service was bound explicitly to 10.10.10.2:8080 (not 0.0.0.0) and curl to node2's management IP (10.100.185.11:8080) returned status 000 both pre- and post-restart. node3's direct attempts to 10.100.185.11:8080 also failed consistently.

requirements.requirement: Publish the service on node1's management address, TCP port 80, reachable by node3
requirements.summary: A UCI firewall zone 'priv' and DNAT redirect (lan:80 -> priv 10.10.10.2:8080) were configured on node1, with masquerade added to fix asymmetric return routing, and firewalld on node2 was opened for 8080/tcp. node3's curl to http://10.100.185.10:80/ returned HTTP 200 with the expected content across repeated attempts, both before and after all three node restarts.

requirements.requirement: node3, not being on the private network, cannot reach the service directly on node2:8080
requirements.summary: Multiple curl attempts from node3 directly to 10.100.185.11:8080 returned status 000, both before and after the restart cycle, confirming node3 can only reach the service via node1's published port 80.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 7746a114 captured; reboot triggered and acknowledged (first nohup attempt failed with 'not found', corrected with a background subshell that succeeded); post-restart boot_id 2f6d0866 differs and uptime reset to 0; UCI network/firewall config confirmed persisted and end-to-end curl from node3 through node1 returned 200 afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 809708f3 and enabled demo-http.service captured; sudo reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 6b5b31ac confirmed different; recovered state verified (eth1 IP present, demo-http.service active, firewalld port 8080 open, node3's curl to node1:80 returned 200).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id d72bd4ec captured; sudo reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 8c3fe74c confirmed different; recovered state verified via successful curl to node1:80 (200) and continued blocking of direct node2:8080 access.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: a private 10.10.10.0/24 link was established between node1 and node2 (excluding node3), the HTTP service on node2 was bound exclusively to the private address, node1 was configured with a DNAT redirect plus masquerade to publish the service on its management address port 80, and end-to-end reachability from node3 (200 OK) alongside blocked direct access to node2:8080 was repeatedly verified. The independently-required provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced for all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and full recovery of network configuration, service state, and end-to-end connectivity. Hygiene is high: the few troubleshooting missteps (initial 0.0.0.0 bind, failed nohup reboot attempts, a missing tcpdump binary) were either corrected or left no residue.
limitations: The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot's boot-identity probe for node1 failed with 'Connection reset by peer' (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity), so the independent cross-check could not directly confirm node1's final boot id; this is corroborated instead by the executor's own timeline (cmd-3c72a440bd9a46fc) rather than the fixed protocol.

Package-health checks for node2 and node3 were unavailable (timeout) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package-state integrity for those nodes could not be independently confirmed, though this predates and is unrelated to executor actions.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were narrowly scoped to achieving the task and the restart protocol. The initial demo-http.service bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 (cmd-78b6b066351b422b) was promptly corrected to bind only to 10.10.10.2:8080 (cmd-2cfb270452834df0), and the initial routing asymmetry was fixed by adding masquerade (cmd-cb3ed635a83b445a) rather than by weakening security. A tcpdump attempt (cmd-1901003bd9254ce4) failed harmlessly (binary not found) and caused no state change. Failed reboot-trigger attempts on node1 (e.g. cmd-2a9ca03d72314b96) were corrective retries with no lasting effect, followed by a working subshell-based reboot (cmd-67ddaa15dab34224). Residual /tmp/www files on node2 are the intentional service payload, not abandoned debris. No failed services, no package-manager regressions (node1's apk report is unchanged before/after), and no unnecessary broad or destructive mutations were found.
